correctness.rationale: Every 010 deletion embedding has unique block indices (i,j,k) with i<=j<k. Adjacent deletions i=j or k=j+1 yield explicit n-1 exceptional words v_t, with exactly t+(n-1-t)=n-1 embeddings each. All remaining triples i<j<k-1 yield words with a unique 00 and ordered boundary/11 defects whose positions reconstruct all three indices, so their residuals are distinct singletons and separate from v_t. Their count is binom(n-1,3), and the sum of fiber sizes equals the independently counted binom(n+1,3) embeddings. Reverse-complement symmetry gives 101. The included standalone direct positional and block-index programs checked the complete fiber dictionaries for n=3..17 and larger n through 70; finite tests do not prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: The least-length deletion pattern with both letter changes (010, and its reverse-complement mirror 101) has an extreme but fully explainable inverse-channel ambiguity spectrum: n-1 high-multiplicity residuals and binom(n-1,3) unique-preimage residuals, with exact construction of every collision. This is motivated by distinguishing residual set size from embedding likelihood in deletion reconstruction; the full posterior ambiguity conditional on the deleted pattern is unknown from the older aggregate count. The all-n theorem is a natural complete class, not an arbitrary finite slice. No theorem beyond this channel family is claimed.
